en: The Text for Worship and Praise at the Nirvana of Śākyamuni Tathāgata; the Text for Worship and Praise at the Anniversary of the Memorial of the Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai.
These are identical in their initial entry into the ritual hall, where one performs three prostrations in unison, burns incense, and kneels alternately. The leader then chants:

With profound reverence, we acknowledge that the Benevolent One appeared in the world, silently realizing the Truth. He dwells as the Honored One throughout the thousand realms and treats the four modes of birth as his children.
His form manifests in accordance with the needs of sentient beings.
The original identity is the body that transcends all marks;
the teachings arise in accordance with the capacities of beings—
how could this differ from the Way beyond words?
Ever since the Wheel of Dharma was first turned, the traces of his transformative teachings have flourished ever more greatly;
it began with the initial discourse on the "half-syllables."
It is like striking away ignorance without weariness;
even for a deposit of a hundred gold pieces,
one would still redeem it with diligent effort.
May all those subject to afflictions be caused to dwell securely within the Tathāgatagarbha;
may the four minds reach fulfillment, and the three virtues be realized.
It means that not a single person is allowed to attain parinirvāṇa alone;
rather, all are brought to parinirvāṇa by means of the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata.
Therefore, entry into nirvāṇa is inconceivable and cannot be grasped by thought.
We, the cranes of the Śāla Grove, have long since departed and thus painfully lost our prior connection;
yet, as the Semblance Dharma still endures, we feel it our duty to follow the Master’s bequeathed instructions.
Now, we encounter the day of mid-spring.
In remembrance of the ritual of bowing the head toward the north, I offer these words like the water-weeds and pond-moss of a mountain stream;
I humbly present this meager offering of sacrifice through the rustic songs and popular verses of Ba.
I briefly set forth my sincere expressions of lamentation.

I only pray that your great compassion will look down upon me with clear discernment. At this point, I prostrate once in total; one must certainly offer this invocation at dawn, while during other times it may be abbreviated.
The invoker chants three times for each name:
With single-minded devotion, we respectfully invoke the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha, the Teacher of Nirvāṇa and the Lord of this Enduring World.
We pray that you will descend to this sacred site and accept our offerings.
With single-minded devotion, I invite the Sūtra-piṭaka, the Dharma-gates expounded during the assembly at the site of Nirvāṇa;
I pray that you descend to this ritual arena to accept my offerings.
With single-minded devotion, I invite the assembly of noble Śrāvakas, Bodhisattvas, and the Saṃgha gathered at the assembly at the site of Nirvāṇa.
I pray that you will descend upon this sacred site and accept my offerings.
With single-minded devotion, I reverently invite the assembly of noble ones, Pratyekabuddhas, and the Sangha gathered at the assembly of the *Nirvāṇa* Sūtra.
I pray that you will descend upon this sacred site and accept my offerings.
With single-minded devotion, I invite the assembly of noble Śrāvaka monks gathered at the site of the *Nirvāṇa* Sūtra.
I pray that you will descend to this ritual arena to accept my offerings.
As for the verses of praise for the Buddha, one may recite them according to what was spoken by Kāśyapa Bodhisattva in the sūtra, or otherwise offer a formal address as one sees fit.
Great King of Physicians who compassionates the world, Whose body and wisdom are both utterly tranquil,
In the selfless phenomena there is a true self— To this Unsurpassed Honored One, I prostrate.
[Recite the verses of praise below, chanting "One Body" up to the word "Śākyamuni," then stand after the prostration and continue with the praises.]

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the World-Honored One of Endurance, the Teacher of Nirvana, Śākyamuni Buddha, who manifested his body when the assembly gathered through the sound and light;

Born from the auspicious river and the firm tree on the first day of the moon, his numinous brilliance and celestial voice pervade the ten directions to summon all living beings and resolve their lingering doubts;
He declares that the Great Awakened One has returned to the ultimate stillness.
The world is adorned with jewels like a blissful land; the blood from human bodies appears like the clouds of offerings from the Tuṣita Heaven.
Yet you remain silent; for a moment, bowing my head, I pay homage with a heart full of sorrow, single-mindedly taking refuge in you.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the World-Honored One of Endurance, the Teacher of Nirvāṇa, Śākyamuni Buddha, who received the offering of food from Cunda;
you who have long realized the essence of Vairocana, yet manifest the ritual of the final passing as a skillful means,
able to produce transformation bodies even upon the tip of a hair, and who now receive these grains of rice from the House of Huā.
Although the six sense-objects are said to be empty and signless, one should know that the five fruits have conditions and a self as their cause.
Now, in honoring the distant ancestors with these offerings of grain, I pray that you may realize the true and eternal, sharing in this wondrous meaning.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge and prostrate to you.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the World-Honored One of Endurance and Teacher of Nirvāṇa, who now lies upon his jeweled bed manifesting illness.
Entrusting Mañjuśrī with the transmission of the True Dharma, he suddenly displays a back ailment to all sentient beings;
bending his arm and lying on his right side like an infant, he withdraws his gaze and remains silent like one who is ill.
Zheng Ren entrusted his hearing to Kāśyapa’s questions; With composure he awaited the arrival of the World-King.
Once more he raised his radiant light to illuminate the great trichiliocosm, Causing all the manifold sufferings within it to be utterly extinguished.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge in and pay homage to him.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One of Endurance, the Teacher of Nirvāṇa, Śākyamuni Buddha, who entered the Moon-Love Samādhi;
out of great compassion, he looked down upon Ajātaśatru, and following Jīvaka’s request, he gave rise to a virtuous mind.
As the deer-throne was again spread forth, the light of the Moon-Love shone, and the king suddenly felt his bodily sores healed by the brocade robes.
Only upon taking refuge in the Buddha do I realize that the heterodox paths were a delusion; only by hearing the sutras do I understand that adverse conditions are empty.
From amidst a thicket of eranda trees, sandalwood has emerged—how marvelous! This analogy illustrates rootless faith;
therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge and prostrate in worship.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One of the Enduring World, the Teacher of Nirvana, Śākyamuni Buddha, who manifests the marks and signs of a human and celestial being.

With hands removing his dharma robes, he extends his body; ascending and descending through space, he performs the four and six circumambulations as he is about to enter the gate of the tranquil Nirvana. Now I behold this assembly adorned with purple-gold radiance.
How could I, with this exhausted body, ever repay the virtue of your cultivated causes? For aeons as numerous as motes of dust, it is difficult to encounter the conditions for transcending the world.
You have earnestly entrusted your final teachings to the future; all should receive the refuge in the Triple Gem.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge and pay homage to you with my head bowed.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One of the Enduring World, Śākyamuni Buddha, the Teacher of Nirvāṇa, who, when contemplating the world in tranquil concentration,
has already revealed the secret treasury in accordance with the needs of beings; now, as he returns to the source,
he again emits a radiance called "Nirvāṇa" at the approach of midnight, pervading all through meditative absorption and transcending them all.
All-encompassing wisdom consists in nothing other than contemplating the true nature of reality; how could sentient beings avoid seeing impermanence?
When the fuel is exhausted and the fire is about to go out, Ānanda’s mind became confused and distraught;
therefore, I single-mindedly take refuge in and prostrate to him.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the World-Honored One of Endurance, the Teacher of Nirvana, Śākyamuni Buddha, who entered the fourth *dhyāna* at the time of his parinirvāṇa.
Having again entered the fourth *dhyāna*, he ceased his final instructions; thus, within *samādhi*, he manifested his passing.
At the twin śāla trees, cranes gathered to cover the golden coffin, and the great earth shook like thunder throughout the *sahasra-lokadhātu*.
Śakra and Brahmā repeatedly offered verses of lamentation; The wicked Māra briefly relieved his anxieties over war.
When the sun of wisdom and the light of compassion cease their shining, When will the long night of ignorance finally dawn?
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge and pay homage to you.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One of Endurance, the Teacher of Nirvāṇa, Śākyamuni Buddha, whose body entered the white cotton shroud within the golden coffin.

The people of the land inquire about the rites for cremation; may the words personally transmitted and entrusted by the Lord of Devas cause them to follow the ceremonial protocols established by the Wheel-Turning King, thereby generating boundless merit for the assembly of Brahmā.
A thousand layers of fine cotton cloth encircle the Sage’s body, and the precious coffin circles the City of the Immortals seven times;
when he is bathed with fragrant waters, all behold his wondrously adorned body remains unimpaired—
therefore, with single-minded devotion, I take refuge and prostrate before him.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One of Endurance, the Teacher of Nirvāṇa, who manifested as Śākyamuni Buddha while within his coffin.
When the Venerable Kāśyapa resided on Vulture Peak, he perceived through meditation that the Buddha had already entered True Reality;
looking afar toward Kuśinagara, he traveled there on foot, arriving just as the funeral rites were being performed.
First, a golden body appeared from within the coffin; next, he prostrated and turned his feet to reveal the wheels upon his soles;
finally, he was able to follow the heart of our sorrowful longing. Because this is the mark of impartial compassion, I single-mindedly take refuge in and pay homage to him with my head bowed.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One of Endurance, the Teacher of Nirvana, Śākyamuni Buddha, as he entered the fragrant tower for cremation.
From the *svastika* upon his chest, the sacred fire flowed forth;
atop the Tower of Universal Fragrance, his true body vanished—his jade-like countenance and golden form utterly gone—yet his silken shroud remains as it was before, like frost-white cotton.
The crystalline relics were distributed throughout the lands, and the stūpas stood tall, manifesting themselves to humans and devas.
We feel shame that we have been born during the remainder of the Semblance Dharma; though our praise is empty, it concerns the legacy of his transformative teachings from that time.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge and pay homage to him.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Sūtra-piṭaka of the Dharma-gates taught at the assembly of *nirvāṇa*.
At its beginning, you expounded wondrous meanings for Cunda; at its end, you delivered subtle words because of Subhadra.
You empowered the *vinaya* to shatter provisional doubts and enabled even icchantikas to give rise to true faith.
Drinking the *amṛta* of clarified butter surpasses all flavors; bathing at the edge of the Bohai Sea encompasses all streams.
May I, throughout all future lives, hear and uphold [this teaching], constantly practicing and studying the perfect *ī* and full *maṇḍala* characters.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge and pay homage.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the assembly of noble śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas gathered at the site of the *Nirvāṇa* Sūtra.

Herein I seek the path to unsurpassed *bodhi*. Having fully assembled the causes for all sentient beings as numerous as motes of dust, do not manifest a mind within the three realms, but regard all living beings with equal affection as if they were your only child.
He leads others toward the Mahāyāna and inspires them to set forth; he guides the lost and the weak, enabling them to know their true home.

A sovereign among men who is like a dragon, appearing at the opportune moment for the benefit of the world in ways inconceivable—I therefore single-mindedly take refuge in him and pay him homage with my head.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the assembly of noble sages and the awakened Saṅgha gathered at the site of Nirvāṇa.
Through causes and conditions, you have deeply entered the realm of saṃsāra; With contemplative insight, you move with ease through the gate of liberation.
Having cultivated merit and wisdom over countless eons, Your supernormal powers can manifest boundless applications.
Having already abandoned the deer-cart and traveled the straight path, unlike the rhinoceros-horn [solitary practitioner] who guards the lone peak,
you have come to meet me between the twin śāla trees; because you appear like a reflection following a form,
I single-mindedly take refuge in you and pay homage with my head bowed.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the assembly of noble Śrāvaka monks gathered at the site of the *Nirvāṇa* Sūtra.
Having tamed their faculties and attained total tranquility, they uphold and disseminate the Bequeathed Teachings.
Having escaped being incinerated within the dilapidated house, they no longer need to gather shards and rubble from the spring pond.
The four fruits of the path are all capable of becoming sons of the Buddha; through the three modes of cultivation, one may together realize the King of Sutras.
The eternal and the impermanent are ultimately identical—this is what is called adorning the twin trees.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge in and pay homage to him.
Having offered praise, kneel again and hold the incense burner as usual, while visualizing clearly and reciting the five repentances.
With a sincere heart, repent:
"I and all sentient beings throughout the ten directions of the Dharma-realm..."
It is solely the source of the purity of one's own mind,
possessing the nature of the wondrous luminosity of all-encompassing wisdom;
before the myriad phenomena had even manifested, it was fundamentally beyond the distinction of sage and ordinary being.
The six delusions form the causes by which one flows into birth and death; consequently,
the pearl between the eyebrows is suddenly lost,
and the film over the eyes increases once more.
Had I not encountered the physician who possesses the clear mirror, I would never have met with the treatment of the golden scalpel.
By what cause did I plant roots in past lives to be born among the ranks of humanity and encounter the Dharma of Śākyamuni?
Although he was counted among the ranks of the bhikṣu-saṃgha,
because his observance of the vinaya was not careful,
the factors of the path were difficult for him to accomplish.
The discourse on the definitive meaning of the One Vehicle has not yet opened true wisdom;
the regulations of the seven groups for preventing wrongdoing [remain unfulfilled].
They frequently commit grave transgressions,
sustaining their bodies with impure things and acting in accordance with ignorance.
With a leak in the life-preserving skin bag,
one truly harbors the anxiety of drowning in the sea;
though the magnificent mansion remains empty.
I would rather accept the gift of entering the Gate;
now, I gaze intently upon Nīvaraṇa and personally perform the practice of *saṃkramaṇa*.
Having confessed the root of one's transgressions,
one then purifies the karmic obstructions;
the Buddha’s compassion covers all universally, and his Dharma-power penetrates subtly and profoundly.
Therefore, I take refuge in you; may you surely grant me your protective mindfulness.
Having completed the repentance, I wholeheartedly take refuge in the Triple Gem and wholeheartedly entreat you.
The Buddhas of the ten directions are eternally quiescent; Each appears in the world for the sake of sentient beings.
Having already attained the fruit of the Way and subdued Māra, They exhort the turning of the Wheel of Dharma to deliver all things.
The auspicious blossom of the udumbara is truly difficult to see; How could the majestic lion’s roar be easily heard?
Even until the time when you manifest parinirvāṇa according to the capacities of beings, we pray that you will extend your kalpa-long lifespan through your great compassion.
Having made this entreaty, we take refuge in the Triple Gem with a sincere heart and rejoice with a sincere heart.
Perfect penetration is already the opening of skillful means; The five vehicles are none other than the convergence into the One Vehicle.
In the past, present, and future, there are those who practice; Their actions of body, speech, and mind are all rejoiced in.
Calling yellow leaves "gold" is a cause that is virtuous; Piling sand to form a stupa, the Way is still accomplished.
Having repented of all instances in the past when I gave rise to a mind of jealousy and anger, and having offered praise and rejoiced in [the merits of others],
I now take refuge in the Triple Gem with a sincere heart and dedicate these merits with a sincere heart.
All meritorious deeds performed in the past and present, I unify and integrate entirely with the wisdom of emptiness.
May all that is done become causes for the four virtues, And not lead to seeking further fruits within the three realms of existence.
If all living beings were not likewise liberated, My mind would never attain bodhi.
Just as all waters flow only toward the great ocean as their source, so too is there no distinction in dedicating [merit] toward the undifferentiated dedication;
having thus dedicated, one takes refuge in the Triple Gem with a sincere heart and makes a vow with a sincere heart.
I vow to cultivate Prajñā within this very body, Constantly contemplating that my Buddha dwells in Nirvāṇa,
A mind that does not depart from the arising of causes and conditions. One then perceives the signless essence within the void,
Whether transcribing upon snow, mountains, trees, or stone, Or lifting the trap and snare amidst the fields.
May all universally aspire to be like Mañjuśrī, simultaneously and clearly realizing the nature of the Tathāgata.
Having made this vow, take refuge in the Triple Gem with a sincere heart.
Circumambulate the ritual site clockwise, recite the *Śūramgama Sūtra*, chant the names of the Buddhas, and withdraw with utmost devotion.
Text for Worship and Praise upon the Parinirvāṇa of Śākyamuni Tathāgata
